theme: ज्ञान और कर्म: अलग दिखने में भी एक लक्ष्य / Knowledge and action: one goal beneath different forms
context: Krishna continues by correcting the idea that knowledge and action are separate, mutually exclusive paths. In the larger context, he is explaining that true inner steadiness does not depend on rejecting the world, but on integrating insight with selfless action.
contextHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो ज्ञान और कर्म को अलग-अलग मानते हैं, वे बालक हैं, पण्डित नहीं. इस प्रसंग में वे बताना चाहते हैं कि वास्तविक सम्यक् स्थिति में कर्म और ज्ञान एक ही लक्ष्य की दो दिशाएँ हैं, न कि विरोधी रास्ते।
sanskritDevanagari:
साङ्ख्ययोगौ पृथग्बालाः प्रवदन्ति न पण्डिताः |
एकमप्यास्थितः सम्यगुभयोर्विन्दते फलम् ||५-४||
transliteration:
sāṅkhyayogau pṛthagbālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ .
ekamapyāsthitaḥ samyagubhayorvindate phalam ||5-4||

wordByWord.meaning: The paths of knowledge and of disciplined action; not necessarily enemies in the practical sense.
The childish, the immature, who divide what is integrally linked.
Speak, declare, or teach in a simplistic way.
Not the wise; not the truly discerning.
One who is established in even one of these paths with integrity.
Fruit, result, or the benefit of the path.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक बहुत सरल लेकिन गहरा है. कृष्ण कहते हैं, 'सांख्य और योग को अलग-अलग बताने वाले बालक हैं, पण्डित नहीं.' यानी जो सोचते हैं कि ज्ञान का मार्ग अलग है और कर्म का मार्ग अलग है, वे अपने मन को छोटी-सी बात में बाँध लेते हैं. यह भाव भी समझना चाहिए कि 'सांख्य' का अर्थ है विवेक, और 'योग' का अर्थ है कर्म को शुद्धता से करने की दिशा. दोनों की अंतर्ज्ञान एक है: आत्मा की पहचान, स्वार्थ का त्याग, और समभाव. अगर कोई एक पक्ष में ठीक तरह स्थिर हो जाता है, तो उसे दोनों का फल मिलता है. यह श्लोक इसलिए महत्वपूर्ण है कि यह न सिर्फ़ दार्शनिक अलगाव को तोड़ता है, बल्कि हमारे जीवन को भी जोड़ता है. हम अक्सर मान लेते हैं कि विचार और व्यवहार अलग हैं. पर अगर विवेक सही है, तो व्यवहार भी सही दिशा लेता है. और अगर कर्म शुद्ध रूप से किया जाए, तो वह ज्ञान को भी पुष्ट करता है. यह एकता का संदेश है, विभाजन का नहीं.
clearEnglish: Krishna here rejects a false dualism: the idea that real knowledge and disciplined action are radically separate. The verse is not denying distinctions; it is denying that they are enemies. A person who is immature says, “This is knowledge, that is action.” But a wise person sees that inner clarity and selfless practice support each other. The key phrase is ekamapyāsthitaḥ—one who is established in even one path, with sincerity, receives the fruit of both. This does not mean that all methods are equally valid in every case, but it does mean that the mature understanding is not captured by rigid separation. A person grounded in wisdom will naturally act with right intention, and one who acts selflessly with integrity will deepen the underlying discernment. In practical life, this invites us to stop treating reflection and behavior as unrelated compartments. Inner seeing and outer living are meant to meet, and when they do, the result is a more coherent path.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Text
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse says that those who divide knowledge and action are childish, while one established in either path rightly gains the fruit of both. The textual emphasis is on non-separation and integration.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Commentary
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The Divine Life Society commentary supports the unity of the paths: those who are truly established in either one attain the fruit of both. It does not treat knowledge and the Yoga of action as separate, opposing paths.

interpretationPerspectives.label: Inference
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A person does not have to choose between theory and practice in a false either/or. A grounded path of action can deepen insight, and insight can refine action.

practicalApplication.label: Unite intention and action
practicalApplication.text: Before an important task, ask: 'What wisdom does this action serve, and what kind of person do I become through doing it?'

practicalApplication.label: Stop fragmented living
practicalApplication.text: If you think of yourself as a 'good thinker' but a careless doer, begin by choosing one responsibility to perform with full attention and without self-display.

reflectionQuestion: In what area of my life am I treating insight and action as separate, and how might bringing them together change my next decision?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मैं अपने जीवन के किस क्षेत्र में विवेक और कर्म को अलग-अलग मानता हूँ, और उन्हें एक साथ लाने से मेरी अगली निर्णय प्रक्रिया कैसे बदल सकती है?
